# Hawks Haulage joins Palletways UK network

Leicester-based logistics provider, Hawks Haulage, has joined the Palletways UK network, marking a key milestone in its strategic growth plans.

Founded in 2019 by Pardeep Virk as a single-truck operation, the company has rapidly grown into a thriving, family-run logistics outfit, now operating a fleet of 35 vehicles and employing 40 staff.

The decision to join Palletways – Europe’s largest express palletised freight network – represents a strategic move to further enhance the business’ offering to customers, while maintaining the personalised service that has underpinned Hawks Haulage’s success.

It comes amid major growth plans which also include further fleet expansions, technological upgrades, staff development and investment in a new state-of-the-art warehouse facility capable of storing up to 2,500 pallets.

This development is set to strengthen the firm’s operational infrastructure, enabling greater efficiency, improving storage solutions and supporting future expansion into integrated logistics services.

# Route2 Logistics opens new Coatbridge depot

 by Transport News | Aug 13, 2026 | Hot News

### Route2 Logistics has officially opened its new depot in Coatbridge, marking a major milestone in the continued growth of the specialist haulage and pallet distribution business.

The new 22,000sq ft facility provides additional warehousing, yard space and vehicle capacity, creating a significant new operational base for Route2 in the West of Scotland and complementing its Dunfermline operation.

The company said the new site creates a stronger Scotland-based network, enabling the business to provide faster lead times, greater capacity and greater flexibility for companies delivering products to customers across Scotland.

Marc Batey, commercial manager at Route2 Logistics, said: “Dunfermline has been our foundation for Route2 in the East of Scotland. Opening a depot further West is the next step in building a stronger, more connected Scottish network.

“Coatbridge puts us right in the heart of the Central Belt and gives us a much stronger position from which to serve customers across Scotland.”

# Six GXO warehouses are changing hands but the trucks are staying put

Pölös Zsófia

Journalist Trans.info | 21.08.2026

DP World is to take over six grocery warehousing operations and more than 2,000 employees from GXO Logistics under a divestment ordered following GXO’s acquisition of Wincanton. 

DP World

The facilities in Doncaster, Rochdale, Charlton, Greenford, Wellingborough and Larne, Northern Ireland, are expected to transfer to DP World in September 2026. Together, they provide more than 2 million sq ft – approximately 186,000 m² – of additional warehouse capacity.

The sites serve Asda, Sainsbury’s and Co-op, storing approximately 46,000 product lines. Their capabilities include ambient, chilled, frozen and bonded storage.

However, GXO will retain the transport operations associated with the sites where applicable, meaning the agreement principally covers the warehousing side of the grocery contracts.

# CEVA Logistics opens Derby distribution centre for UK eCommerce 

 

> CEVA Logistics opens Derby distribution centre for UK eCommerce 

CEVA Logistics has opened a new 508,000-square-foot distribution centre in Derby, expanding its UK contract logistics network to support growing demand from the eCommerce sector.

The facility is scheduled to become fully operational in August 2026. It will provide storage, handling and distribution services for global eCommerce customers, helping speed up deliveries across the UK.

The new operation is expected to create around 300 jobs, strengthening the regional logistics sector while supporting CEVA’s continued investment in the UK market.

The warehouse was designed with sustainability and scalability in mind. It has achieved BREEAM Excellent and EPC A+ certifications and features a rooftop solar installation to reduce energy consumption.
